body:
Thanks for the updates! Could you check here again?

When the user sets `shopt -u extquote`, `"${PS1//[!$'\n']}"` (which is quoted inside `"..."`) fails to properly remove the characters with Bash <= 5.1 (I think Bash-5.2's behavior is a bug). It leaves `$`, `'`, `\`, and `n` and removes everything other than them.

An easy way is to use variable assignment such as `nlns=${...}` because the right-hand side of the assignments is not subject to pathname expansions and word splitting so does not need to be quoted (unless it contains the shell special delimiters like `;|&<>`).

```suggestion
            local nlns=${PS1//[!$'\n']}
            bleopt prompt_rps1="$nlns$(::STARSHIP:: prompt --right --terminal-width="$COLUMNS" --status=$STARSHIP_CMD_STATUS --pipestatus="${STARSHIP_PIPE_STATUS[*]}" --jobs="$NUM_JOBS" --cmd-duration=$STARSHIP_DURATION)"
```

If you don't like it, maybe there is another approach, e.g., to save and restore the state of `shopt -u extquote`, etc.

Maybe for consistency this would be more appropriate? 
```suggestion
    if [[ "${#BLE_PIPESTATUS[@]}" -gt "${#STARSHIP_PIPE_STATUS[@]}" ]]; then
```

I'd say it doesn't work.

Inside ble.sh, `PIPESTATUS` contains a pipe status of random commands, so its content is unpredictable. With the current implementation of ble.sh, `PIPESTATUS` seems to be single-valued within the hook functions, but that can change in the future. Even if `PIPESTATUS` is ensured to be single-valued, the above condition doesn't work when the real pipe status of the previous user command is also single-valued (which is the majority of the cases).

Also, as far as the hook functions are called by ble.sh, `BLE_PIPESTATUS` is ensured to exist. Ah, but wait. An old version of ble.sh may not have the support. I've now checked the git blame, and `BLE_PIPESTATUS` was added two years ago. If we would care about it, I think the check could be

```suggestion
    if [[ ${BLE_ATTACHED-} && ${#BLE_PIPESTATUS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
```
